title: Dhamaal 4 Trailer Drops With a 60-Foot Waterfall Reveal — Ajay Devgn and Company Are Back for Maximum Chaos
excerpt: The fourth instalment of Bollywood's wildest comedy franchise launches its trailer at Imagicaa with trademark spectacle, hitting theatres July 10
body:
Bollywood's most chaotic franchise just pulled off the most Bollywood stunt imaginable: launching a trailer not at a press conference, not at a multiplex, but at the base of a sixty-foot waterfall at Imagicaa amusement park, with the poster cascading down the falls like some kind of fever dream designed by a marketing team on Red Bull and good vibes. Welcome to Dhamaal 4.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=lFJZIKeSflQ

The trailer, clocking in at a meaty three minutes and thirty seconds, dropped today (June 12) and it is exactly what you would expect from a franchise that has never pretended to be anything other than pure, uncut comic mayhem. Ajay Devgn leads the pack once more, reuniting with Arshad Warsi, Riteish Deshmukh, and Jaaved Jaaferi — the four horsemen of Bollywood slapstick — in a treasure-hunt adventure that appears to involve jungles, explosions, absurd disguises, and at least one sequence that defies the laws of physics in ways Newton would find personally offensive.

A Cast That Keeps Growing

Director Indra Kumar has stacked the bench this time. Alongside the original quartet, Dhamaal 4 brings in Sanjay Mishra (whose deadpan timing alone is worth the ticket price), Esha Gupta, Sanjeeda Shaikh, Anjali Anand, Ravi Kishan, Upendra Limaye, and Vijay Patkar. That is not a cast — it is a small army. And in the Dhamaal universe, more actors means more chaos, which is precisely the point.

The franchise has always operated on a simple thesis: throw as many absurd situations at the screen as possible, keep the energy manic, and trust that audiences will show up for the ride. It has worked three times running. The original Dhamaal (2007) was a sleeper hit. Double Dhamaal (2011) doubled down on the formula. Total Dhamaal (2019) crossed the two-hundred-crore mark. The trajectory suggests the appetite for this brand of unhinged comedy is not slowing down.

Summer Blockbuster Season Heats Up

The July 10 release date is strategic. Originally slated for July 17, Dhamaal 4 moved up a week after Alia Bhatt's Alpha — the first female-led YRF Spy Universe film — shifted to July 3. That gives Dhamaal 4 a clear runway before anything else big lands, and slots it perfectly into the summer holiday corridor when families are most likely to pile into theatres for something loud, silly, and entirely calorie-free.

This is also a franchise that travels exceptionally well with diaspora audiences. The Dhamaal films are the kind of movies NRIs watch in packed weekend shows at Cinemark and AMC — not for prestige, not for awards bait, but for the communal experience of laughing yourself stupid with a room full of desis who have been working too hard all week and just need ninety minutes of pure nonsense. There is genuine value in that. Not everything needs to be Oppenheimer.

The Imagicaa Launch — Peak Bollywood Marketing

About that waterfall reveal. Imagicaa, the Khopoli amusement park that has become something of a Bollywood promotional playground, hosted the entire cast for the trailer unveiling. The sixty-foot poster cascading down the waterfall was theatrics of the highest order — silly, spectacular, and perfectly on brand for a franchise that treats subtlety as a personal insult. Say what you will about Indra Kumar, the man understands his audience. You do not sell Dhamaal with a sober press conference. You sell it with a waterfall.

What To Expect

If the trailer is any indication, Dhamaal 4 is not reinventing the wheel. It is polishing the wheel, putting spinners on it, and sending it downhill at irresponsible speed. The treasure-hunt premise gives the ensemble an excuse to globe-trot through increasingly ridiculous setpieces, and the chemistry between Devgn, Warsi, Deshmukh, and Jaaferi remains the franchise's secret weapon — four actors who genuinely seem to enjoy each other's company on screen, which makes the comedy feel organic rather than manufactured.

July 10. Mark it. Bring the family. Leave your cynicism at home.
